label: GO step after an unrewarded trial, late in the episode, when the policy strongly favors a1
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass), almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded (99.5% of mass with prev_reward==0, never with in_rew==1), and when the model is about to choose a1 with a large policy logit (73% of mass in the top choice bin, choice > 8.07; 94% of mass on model_act==1). It never fires before episode trial ~30, and its rate climbs steadily through trials 40-99, so it looks like a late-episode clock signal. It is also enriched after rare transitions (prev_common==0, 3x lift) and when S1 is the good state. The predicate uses only observed or computed variables: the reward input and the agent own policy logit. Dev split: P=0.92, R=0.70, F1=0.80, mass recall 0.74. Test F1 is about 0.77, so recall is incomplete. Loosening to choice > 4 raises mass recall to 0.88 but drops precision to 0.64. Most missed activations are weak firings at GO with a moderate a1 logit, or rare firings after rewarded trials or when choosing a2. It does not fire at D1 or D2, after rewarded trials, or early in the episode.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over last trial (GO: a1 S2 u, a2 S2 u, ?) and trial before (GO: a1 S2 u, a1 S1 u, a1 S1 r); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO & ep_dec=9, phase=GO & ep_dec=8, phase=GO & ep_dec=7.
